articles.title: Plans for Demolition of Flats in Lower Falinge Resurface
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has revealed new plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, sparking distress among remaining residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, which contain 126 homes, as part of a redevelopment project. The proposal aims to replace the existing buildings with 270 new homes, including a mix of flats and houses, on land between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street.

The maisonette blocks known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, and Vaynor are set for demolition, with only the Zedburgh block currently occupied. Andy Roche, a resident of the Zedburgh block since 1988, expressed his distress over the news, stating that he and his partner are the last remaining tenants in the block. He claimed that the eviction is taking a toll on their health, as both he and his partner are autistic.

RBH previously faced a legal challenge that halted demolition plans last year, but the new proposals have emerged following consultations with local residents. Despite this, Roche feels that the concerns of current residents have not been adequately addressed. He has been offered alternative housing options by RBH but believes none match his current living situation.

The estate has seen significant changes over the years, with previous phases of redevelopment already delivering 100 new homes since 2012. However, the area remains marked by its history of deprivation, having been labelled a 'sink estate' by former Prime Minister David Cameron in 2016. Residents like Roche lament the loss of community and the decline of the estate, which once thrived with families and children.
